Episode 184. Beyond Fate (22)
Half.
Approximately half of the enemies had vanished during the short time Murakan remained on the battlefield.
Meri, Tona, and Yona cut the necks of those who had been the previous head families.
Even though the Black Shackles had already disappeared, they could not offer even a decent resistance.
The enemies' formation was collapsing. The allies were desperately plunging into the weak points, swinging their swords, and shooting magic.
The melee continued again.
However, now the temporary alliance clearly had the upper hand.
Although there were many casualties, many more enemies were falling.
"Victory is near, stay focused until the end!"
"Is there still no news of the 12th Legion?"
Whenever there was a break, even for a moment, the allies would look over towards the soul energy barrier that held Jin and Hyungshin.
The barrier was noticeably smaller than when Murakan had first breached it.
It looked too narrow for two people to stand.
'Did Jin enter a new sub-space with Hyungshin...'
Valeria narrowed her brows as she examined the log window.
The log window described that Jin and Hyungshin had left the battlefield.
She was worried.
She had used the wave tracking synchronization device and even called Murakan, so now Jin had no more tricks up his sleeve.
Enya, who noticed her worry, grabbed Valeria's hand.
"Jin Gongja will definitely return."
Valeria opened her eyes wide for a moment and then smiled at Enya.

"Wow, it's a rare sight to see Valeria smile. You're already pretty, but you're even more beautiful when you smile... Should I start another fan club? Anyway, don't worry about Jin Gongja, help me with this."
Enya pulled out a 'mirror' from her pocket.
"The soul energy wrapping Lam is continuously shrinking. If we use a fireproof barrier enhanced with the mirror, we can delay it a bit."
Along with the soul energy gradually tightening, Lam was slowly sinking.
It wasn't due to some control lowering its altitude.
It was losing its functions due to Murakan's breath and the ongoing battle's destruction.
People and monsters on the crashing giant ship.
Hoping that all the people would survive safely, Enya opened the mirror.
Valeria was assisting her, reading the flow of that infinite magical power instead of her.
Gradually, the traces of the sub-space where Jin and Hyungshin were trapped were getting farther away.
Even as Lam was sinking, the traces of the subspace remained motionless in the sky.
Thinking about Jin fighting alone inside, his colleagues were faithfully carrying out their respective roles.
Jin was facing Hyungshin.
At first, it was a giant monster similar to Glyiek, and after fusing with Lam, it took the form of a devil with horns and wings steeped in chaos.
Now, Hyungshin took on the form Jin was most familiar with.
Calmly settled black hair, cold and solid gaze, a straight back that wouldn't bend to anything.
The image of a human who had led the family as the owner of Runckandell for a long time.
Unlike when he faced young Rosa in Hyungshin's castle, Jin was no longer surprised by Hyungshin's transformation.
"Hyungshin, I somehow knew you'd be like this if I followed you in..."
There was no hint of trembling in Jin's sword pointed at Hyungshin.
The emotion that had just risen passionately had become a will to kill the opponent like a tempered sword.
Hyungshin looked at Jin silently for a while.
Jin could feel that no aura was being formed.
The same went for magic and soul energy.
In this subspace, no special power could be used.
But he was not afraid.
Even if he had to fight with his bare hands without a sword, he was certain that he would not die here.
"What a desolate landscape."
Hyungshin spoke, with a vacant voice like a condemned prisoner who had accepted his fate and stood on the scaffold.
The subspace where the two were standing was unlike anything they had experienced before, it was completely white. A wide and empty white desert.
This place is the end of Hyungshin's inner world, his unconscious.
"I'm suddenly curious about what your space looks like. It won't be as empty and cold as mine."
"I haven't lived like you."
There was no anger in Jin's reply.
"No. Our lives are still similar, younger brother. It's just not completely the same."
"Where do you think that small difference came from?"
"Do you want to say it's the fighting spirit?"
"That's right."

"How harsh. Even if I were reborn, I don't think I could live a more fierce life than I do now. I can't make the choice not to become Hyungshin. For the family, I really dedicated everything... I spent my whole life controlling all desires, never prioritizing individual over the family, never complaining once. In that lonely and cold time."
"You went about it the wrong way."
"What is the right way? And can a criminal like me do it too? Even if I can't get a chance to live a new life by returning with my memories like you?"
Jin was not taken aback even when the monster mentioned his return. He had a suspicion that death had revealed one secret to the god that should now disappear.
"There's something I've always wondered about. In your past life, what was the reason for expelling me and cutting off the energy for two days?"
The monster chuckled lightly.

"You're asking the obvious. Do you think I'm not a human? I also feel sadness, fall into depression, and writhe in agony. I want to be with my husband, I want to hug my children. But in doing so, the Rune candle family cannot become stronger. It's not the way of the Rune candle, it's the way of an ordinary family."
Jin closed his eyes tightly for a moment.

"I'm not a monster, little one. I was just thrown into a situation where I had to become a monster. Even before accepting chaos, I was already a monster. I had no choice but to be. It's not about whether I chose it or not. I never had the power to decide my own life."
That's the difference between you and me.
Transparent tears flowed from the monster's eyes as he continued.
"I did my best to fight against life, but I lost. I could not overcome the inevitable fate, destiny. It's the difference caused by the capacity I was born with and the opportunities given."
The monster slowly pulled out his sword from his scabbard.

"I'm not resentful. Not everyone can realize their dreams, and not everyone can fulfill their given duties. There are things that can't be helped no matter how fierce. I certainly don't want to make excuses. I just want to tell someone, to you... that's all."
"If you failed as a human rather, if you had stayed a person and not become a monster. Even if that eventually led the family to ruin. I might have felt a little sympathy for your story."
"Maybe."
"I would have tried to understand, even if I couldn't forgive you."

"But even now I don't want that. I no longer know what human feelings are, what choices a human should naturally make. I don't want to deny my brutal past, and I certainly don't intend to justify my sins."
I just want to break down and fall while fighting with you now...
Clang-!
The sword fell into Jin's chest.
It was heavy.
Jin didn't know if the sword was heavy or if something else was heavy.
He just had to throw it off, cut it, stab it.

"Little one. This fight is more of a blessing for me. My last humanity cursed me as it died in your arms. I desperately hope that curse will be realized. Do you know why? Because pain is better than loneliness."
This time, Jin thrust his knife into the monster's throat.
Blood stained the knife that grazed his throat. The hot, red drops of blood kept blurring his vision.
It felt like he was cutting a person, not a monster.
The sense that he could finally make a decisive break with a human, not a monster.
But Jin thought this was not a 'match'.
The monster had, in fact, already lost to life even before giving birth to Jin. She was already as monstrous as any other person before Jin had grown up.
It was impossible to defeat someone who had already lost a long time ago.
That person is not here.
Of the two interlocked swords, one belongs to a human living in the present, and the other is nothing more than a trace of a person who disappeared long ago.
In the relentless exchange of blows, wounds multiplied on both Jin and the monster. They were spilling each other's blood.
To the point where they wanted to stop fighting.
The monster lunged with her sword desperately. Even as she was torn apart, she showed no hesitation.
Jin thought that she was selfish to the end, as if your heart becomes strange when your parents die despite the brutal abuse.
Just like unavoidable agony comes.
They didn't know how long they had fought.
Jin, with one knee bent, leaned on his sword and looked down at the monster.
"Huuk, keuk......"
The fallen monster gasped for air. She kept opening her mouth as if she wanted to say something, but only bloody foam came out instead of words.
Jin didn't have the strength left to cut her last breath. He had to watch the monster's final moments while catching his breath.
The monster's consciousness was fading away.
Jin never took his eyes off her.
He held onto his fading consciousness to witness her death.
In the end, the monster couldn't leave a last word for Jin.
The moment the monster's breath stopped.
Huaaaak……!
Suddenly, a bright white light flashed, and Jin reflexively closed his eyes.
When he opened his eyes, the blue sky of Hupester, which he hadn't seen in a long time, was enveloping him.
Jin was falling towards the ground, unable to move a finger.
He had escaped from the void.
One by one, people's voices came to Jin's falling ears. He could hear the mournful cries of his comrades.
A lump of warmth, like a spring breeze, enveloped him.
It was Valeria's magic.
Jin was gently pulled by the wind magic and fell into Valeria's arms.
And then Jin could see.
He saw the desperate faces of Valeria and his comrades, who were inspecting his face and screaming something.
And he saw the Garden of Swords stretching out behind them.
Seeing that landscape still intact, Jin closed his eyes.
